slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
AAS: if two angles and a non-included side of one triangle are equal to those of another, the triangles are congruent.

Proof: the angle sum fixes the third angle (180 minus the other two), so the third angles are equal too, and ASA applies.

HL: if the hypotenuse and a leg of one right triangle are equal to those of another right triangle, the triangles are congruent.

Proof idea: place the triangles so the equal legs line up and the right angles form a straight line. The two hypotenuses make an isosceles triangle, so the base angles are equal, and AAS finishes it. HL needs the right angle; without it, this is the SSA case, which fails.
